display_name: The Osa battery's emission regimes (режим излучения)
notes: How long the radars may radiate, ordered from above and passed down by voice (docs/crew/16_EMISSION.md; simcore/emission_regime.hpp). The battery commander's decision fixes the measures against jamming and anti-radiation missiles and each launcher's order of search and fire (voenizdat_osa_1991 p243); under the threat of ARMs the radars radiate as little as possible (p262); above the battery the military district's signal frees the wartime frequencies and peacetime radiation keeps to permitted frequencies and directions (pp. 208-211). The four regimes and the words for them are SAM3D's: the textbook gives the least emission against ARMs, not a list of regimes. The battery's orders on its net use ПТ-1's groups (data/command/talk_tables.json), which are placeholders.
source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p243, p262, pp. 208-211; the regimes as a list and their names: sam3d

free.notes: The radars radiate as the fight needs (the readiness drill: the search radar on at the halt).

on_turns.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p262 (the search transmitter's high voltage on for 2 antenna turns, the figure for the least emission); vr_1985_plss (transmitter discipline: every newly switched-on source detected within seconds)

off_turns.source: estimate (against direction finding with no ARM threat the bursts can be rarer than the 3-4 turns of p262; the campaign's search bursts were 10-40 s off, 5-22 turns)

limited.notes: Against direction finding with no ARM threat: the search transmitter in bursts while no hostile is within the tracking radar's reach; on all the time once one is.

on_turns.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p262 («включения высокого напряжения передатчика СОЦ через 3—4 оборота антенны на 2 оборота»)

off_turns.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p262 (3-4 turns off; the low end, as doctrine arm_search_off_turns)

arm.notes: The whole least emission of p262: the search transmitter 2 turns on after every 3-4 off and off while the tracking radar holds a stable track alone; the tracking transmitter on only from Table 7.3's range and off after the missile's burst; the TV for tracking.

silent.notes: Both radars off: the TV and the battery's designations only (samsim_osa p33-35).

relay_s.source: estimate (the battery commander hears the regiment's order, decodes the group and says it on the battery net)

pass_on_s.source: estimate (the vehicle commander takes the battery's order off his headset and tells the crew on the intercom)

repeat_s.source: estimate (an order not heard by a launcher is said again: rrs_1986, a main station repeats until it is received)

arm_on_report_s.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p243 (the measures against ARMs are the battery commander's decision) and p262 (the least emission under the threat); the delay: estimate
arm_on_report_s.notes: A launcher's report of an ARM attack puts the battery under the least emission this long after the battery commander hears it, if it isn't silent or under it already.

remind_quiet_s.source: estimate (the commander reminds the radar seats of the regime when a hostile appears after this long without one)

breach_turns.source: estimate (a burst this many turns longer than ordered, with nothing tracked, and the commander tells the senior operator again)
